offence_severity: Rigorous imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs.2000/- under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC
physical_harm: The deceased suffered burn injuries covering almost the entire body except the legs below the knees, with approximately 85% burns. She was also beaten up mercilessly by her husband before being set on fire.
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 498-A and 302 read with Section 34 IPC; both offences were upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused planned and executed the act of setting the deceased on fire with kerosene oil, indicating premeditation
motive: Harassment and cruelty due to dowry demands
key_evidence_accepted: The dying declaration of the deceased is fully acceptable since the Judicial Magistrate (PW-10) reached the hospital, satisfied herself through the statement of the duty doctor that the deceased was conscious and fit to make a statement, and recorded her statement in the form of question and answers.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, including the Judicial Magistrate and the duty doctor, as credible and reliable, noting that the deceased was fit to make a statement and that the procedure followed was proper.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 14.05.1998; Trial judgment: 27.09.2001; High Court decision: 15.05.2006; Supreme Court decision: 22.03.2013
legal_representation: R.N. Kush, S.K. Sabharwal for the Appellants; Kamal Mohari Gupta, Mohd. Zahid Hussain for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered on 17.05.1998; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence; High Court: Confirmed conviction and dismissed appeal; Supreme Court: Dismissed appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased, Kailash, was harassed and killed by the accused, Rakesh and his mother-in-law, Ram Piari, for dowry. The trial court convicted the accused primarily based on the dying declaration of the deceased.
defence_argument: The appellants-accused contended that the dying declaration was not reliable and that the accused-husband's burn injuries made it improbable that he set the deceased on fire.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a dying declaration is acceptable in view of the facts of the case and that the prosecution must establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution established its case beyond reasonable doubt, and the courts below correctly convicted the accused based on the dying declaration and other evidence.
